claims.text: The launch signaled a shift toward frontier reasoning models that integrate vision natively into the model architecture rather than bolting it on, while also featuring native tool use (such as web search and code interpreter) trained directly into the system [Source: ev-1].

Strategically, with GPT-5 not yet shipping, OpenAI used this release to defend its position at the reasoning-model frontier against DeepSeek's R1 cost shock and Anthropic’s push in agentic coding [Source: ev-1].

claims.text: To support this direction, o3 was priced at $10 per million input tokens and $40 per million output tokens, while o4-mini was priced more accessibly at $1.10 per million input tokens and 4.40 dollars per million output tokens [Source: ev-1].

witness.reason: claim figures absent from the evidence — untraced: 3, 4

claims.text: The launch also highlighted advancements in efficiency and performance through a technique called budget forcing, which uses a fixed maximum thought budget with task-adaptive compute to allow harder questions to think longer [Source: ev-1].
Additionally, it marked OpenAI’s first private chain-of-thought policy, where reasoning tokens are not exposed to API callers [Source: ev-1].

In terms of capability, o3 set a record on the ARC-AGI benchmark, achieving approximately 87.5% on ARC-AGI-1 at high compute—reaching or exceeding the ~85% human baseline for the first time among models [Source: ev-1].
